propositions: The existing check_raw_git_writes.py gate (R1/R2) enforces no-raw-subprocess-git but misses non-atomic mutation sequences composed by sanctioning individual primitives at module granularity, violating the protocol rule that tracker mutations must go through atomic locked transactions.

Rule R3 (seam composition) must fire when git_adapter mutation primitives are called from outside the sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), with receiver binding resolved via import statements and dynamic-loader module-path strings, excluding reads and non-git-adapter methods.

Two out-of-transaction sites require durable reasoned inline markers rather than debt baseline: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) selectively stages 5 files to avoid sweeping in .bridge_state/last-pass.json, and __main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks) uses a detached temp index with CAS ref-advance for concurrency safety.

The implementation adds R3 to the existing checker with new unit tests covering false-positive floor, sanctioned entry, marker semantics, and dynamic-loader binding, and refactors __main__.py's pass-lock logic into _pass_lock_lifecycle.py to stay under module-size limits.

All sanctioned mutation-primitive calls must carry an explicit # raw-git-ok: <reason> marker (line or enclosing function), reusing the existing marker vocabulary, and the gate must enumerate zero unsanctioned violations after blocker tickets close.

R3's first run on the real tree enumerated exactly 7 hits across 2 functions with zero false positives, both sites took durable reasoned markers as planned, and all local gates (lint, typecheck, unit tests, check_raw_git_writes.py) exit 0.
